notes.title: Big Playtest Update
notes.notes:
Changelog v0.40:

- New Audio ( now some characters respond to us - Worker, Spearman, Warrior )
- Fixes with saving ( group controls, recruitment queue )
- Fixes with bugs ( sometimes button recruit was disabled )
- Fixes with camera rotations
- Update translations
- Move camera to selected Unit ( you can move to your unit by clicking its small icon in Unit Panel Info )
- Notifications ( Popups in right up corner show basic informations about current events. You can interact with some of them by clicking - New Building, No food in Tavern, Max Population Reached )
- Easier building with multiple workers
- Small changes in tutorial ( disabling Hp Bars in start workers - we can't control them :D, disabling Altar mechanics until we upgrade it )
- Tavern now can store 100% items ( last time we locked it on 70% of max storage capacity, now we move it back to 100% )
- Smaller fixes and upgrades

We know there are some problems with sharing knowledge about game mechanics. We are aware of this and soon we will come back with good solution. In fact we already have a plan how to fix it but we need some time in order to implement it 😄

notes.title: VIKING VILLAGE
notes.notes:
[h1]Hello Slavic Builders![/h1]

Today we have great news for you! The Vikings just arrived in our game!
Have you seen that one of the biggest myths about Vikings is that they wore horned hats?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40115388/0efa405ffcb34ba7385d11d9f6b8c97848f0bc9b.png[/img]

There were no horns on Viking helmets - but the myth of the devil's headgear is still fine.
The "blame" for the creation of this myth is probably the costume designer Cami Emil Doepler, who wanted to attract the attention of viewers with his characteristic Viking figure.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40115388/d60f7456a8f2cf3ebedc85cb29199129cbf3813d.png[/img]

Meanwhile, helmets from the period of Viking expeditions do not have any horns. Rather, they are fairly simple headgear with no eye protection and no ornaments. Let us know if you know about it!

[url=https://discord.gg/fPDHKX76JD][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40115388/ec29dadf15db1421b9984cc1234b28314f448a34.png[/img][/url]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1570220/Mythos_Slavic_Builder/

notes.title: VILLAGE LIFE WOOD CHOPPING
notes.notes:
[h2]Hello Slavic Builders![/h2]

Today you may take a look at our first tests of the resource gathering mechanics.🪓
In Mythos: Slavic Builder, you can assign selected dwellers to any work building so they start their new job. They will bustle to give you stable production, collecting materials, processing them and filling your storages with them, until they get hungry, but we'll talk about it on another occasion.😊

[previewyoutube=iCj7J4E1uKQ;full][/previewyoutube]

The majority of raw materials, such as wood and berries, will be gathered by workers directly from the sources found on the map, however, sometimes you will need more advanced resources to keep your people safe and thriving. Your skilled specialists will work along the entire production chains to transform one material into another, such as burning clay into bricks, forging steel into weapons or grinding grain into flour which can then be used to bake bread.🍞

Our idea was to create a settlement in which the dwellers would be independently roaming between the buildings, giving the impression of a village that lives its own life, in which something is constantly happening, like in an anthill. ❤️

[h1]How do you like it? Please let us know in the comments! :)[/h1]

[url=https://discord.gg/YK24vEreZH][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40115388/ec29dadf15db1421b9984cc1234b28314f448a34.png[/img][/url]

notes.title: MEET THE LESHEN
notes.notes:
[h1]Hello Slavic Builders![/h1]

Today we'd like to introduce you to Leshen, whom you could already see in the trailer of Mythos: Slavic Builder.

The forest was one of the most important elements in the life of ancient Slavs. It met their basic needs - it was a source of food and wood for building shelters. But on the other hand it was also scary - wild predators and dense thickets where it was easy to get lost meant that people often did not return from the woods.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40115388/08517171fff43745577701def5e7c92d4ead8d4f.png[/img]

The Slavs believed that this duality of the forest materialized in the form of Leshen (the forest man or the forest keeper). Leshen looked like a man who was a part of the woods, he took care of the trees and grazed the forest animals, in which he was helped by his subordinate wolves. He could jealously protect his domane, or help people when he felt like it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40115388/e8d5b9de6e40338dd4af211eb8f1be05a2439721.jpg[/img]

In Mythos: Slavic Builder, forests also help to provide the player's settlement with a supply of basic resources for survival, and some of them may belong to a Leshen. Would you try to stand up to Leshen and his wolves? Or maybe you’d rather make regular sacrifices on his altar to win the favor of the protector of the forest, permission to use his goods, or even an offer to join your party?
